correctness.rationale: The source planar homogeneous cubic equations yield exactly dr/dt=r^3(-a+b cos2theta), dtheta/dt=r^2. Integrating d(log r^2)/dtheta gives r^2=C exp(-2a theta+b sin2theta). The strictly increasing integral I(theta)=int_-infty^theta exp(2a u-b sin2u) du yields exact physical-time I(theta(t))=I0+Ct. Its positive pi-periodic factor G establishes global invertibility. F=e^(b sin2theta)G gives the exact expression t r^2=(1-I0/(I0+Ct))*Phi(log(I0+Ct)); bounded smooth derivatives prove O(1/t). The linear equation F'=(-2a+2b cos2theta)F+1 proves constancy iff b=0. Continuous periodic mapping produces the exact entire interval of accumulation points; logarithmic Cesaro averaging yields the universal profile-pushforward law. Sympy verifies Cartesian/polar identities and high-precision independent quadrature checks 35 finite identities from the standalone checker; experiments are not a proof.

originality.rationale: The full motivating paper gives the homogeneous cubic polynomial, polar reduction, global GAS and Lyapunov obstruction, but not an original-time logarithmically periodic amplitude profile, a full radial limit interval, or a log-time occupation law. The closest published homogeneous star-node return theorem requires a positive linear star-node term and treats a nonzero attracting cycle; it does not establish the zero-linear-part, physical-time algebraic decay profile. The closest cubic Lienard theorem proves a constant normalized radial limit in a different system. Exact statement/implication comparisons of accessible primary sources and repeated semantic research searches found no stronger covering result. Older homogeneous-focus reductions may subsume this quadrature, which is documented as residual risk.

value.rationale: The new model is the canonical recent counterexample to polynomial Lyapunov converse theory. While its global stability was proved, the sharp physical-time radial relaxation law was not supplied. The nonconstant logperiodic envelope provides a mathematically meaningful distinction between convergence to a point and existence of a sharp constant asymptotic radial prefactor; it resolves the complete natural limit-set problem for the t*r(t)^2 observable for every parameter and nonzero orbit, with a universal log-time statistical law and the exact boundary b=0. This is not an arbitrary parameter slice or renaming of an existing formula. Standard polar integrability is credited rather than claimed novel.
